fullName.question: What is your full legal name
fullName.explanation: Use the name that appears on your ID or Social Security card

dateOfBirth.question: What is your date of birth

address.question: What is your home address
address.explanation: Use the address where you currently live, even if it is temporary
address.example: 123 Main St, Apt 4, Salt Lake City, UT 84101

householdSize.question: How many people live in your household
householdSize.explanation: Count people who buy and cook together as one household
householdSize.example: If you live with 2 roommates but buy your own food, answer 1

monthlyIncome.question: How much money do you earn each month before taxes
monthlyIncome.explanation: Include wages, tips, and any other income. Use the amount before taxes are taken out
monthlyIncome.example: If you earn $15 an hour and work 80 hours a month, answer 1200

employer.question: Who is your employer
employer.explanation: Enter the name of the business or person you work for. If you have more than one job, list your main one

payFrequency.question: How often do you get paid
payFrequency.explanation: Choose how often you receive a paycheck from your main job
payFrequency.example: If you get paid every other Friday, choose biweekly

workHours.question: How many hours do you work each week
workHours.explanation: Use your average if your hours change from week to week
workHours.example: If you work 15 hours one week and 25 the next, answer 20

monthlyRent.question: How much do you pay for rent or mortgage each month
monthlyRent.explanation: Include only your share if you split housing costs with people outside your household
monthlyRent.example: If your rent is $1,200 and you split it evenly with one roommate, answer 600

paysUtilities.question: Do you pay for utilities separately from your rent
paysUtilities.explanation: Utilities include heating, cooling, electricity, gas, water, and phone
paysUtilities.example: If you pay your own electric bill, answer yes

isStudent.question: Are you currently enrolled in college or a training program
isStudent.explanation: This includes community college, university, and trade or vocational school
isStudent.example: If you take classes at a community college, answer yes

enrollmentStatus.question: Are you enrolled full-time or part-time
enrollmentStatus.explanation: Half-time or more usually means 6 or more credit hours per term. Check with your school if you are not sure
enrollmentStatus.example: If you take 12 credits this semester, choose full-time

hasWorkStudy.question: Do you have a federal or state work-study job
hasWorkStudy.explanation: Work-study is a job you got through your financial aid package
hasWorkStudy.example: If your financial aid award letter lists work-study and you have a campus job through it, answer yes

hasChildUnder6.question: Do you take care of a child under 6 years old
hasChildUnder6.explanation: The child must live with you and be part of your household
hasChildUnder6.example: If your 4-year-old daughter lives with you, answer yes

inCTEProgram.question: Are you in a career or technical education program
inCTEProgram.explanation: These programs train you for a specific job, like nursing, welding, or medical assisting
inCTEProgram.example: If you are in a certified nursing assistant program, answer yes
